title: FIG. 03 · The Painted Chip
summary: Round 2's four-number plate is back as it was; the square of dots in the centre is now a painted block of 100 — red paints the share for whichever number you pick, the empty share is hatched like a cut surface on a technical drawing, and one line says what the 100 stands for.
story: After the reframe says most teams are fixing the wrong layer, this section brings in the market's own published research as outside proof, paints each finding as a share you can read at a glance, and hands the letter its cue with 'Not one of them moves with more activity.'
motion: Standalone mockup: the head plays as usual. The plate's lines draw, the four readings come in with their numbers rising from below, and the four corner marks register. The centre's vertical hairline then carries on down and lands on the top edge of the block, the block's pale ground paints down from that edge, and the scale's ticks calibrate from 0 up to 100. Finally the red rises from the base to 17. All of this is done by about 2s.

The control is then demoed once: 95:5 at about 2.4s, 77 at 3.3s, 53 at 4.3s and back to 17 at 5.2s. Each change is one even move (0.65s in the demo, 1.1s when you click). At 95:5 the label '5 buying now' prints in the pale sliver as the red arrives. Everything has settled by about 5.9s, and nothing moves after that.

Interaction: press a big number (anywhere on its reading works). Hovering a number previews its reading in the block, and a grey line marks that reading. Moving away returns to the pressed one. The arrow keys step through the four numbers, and Home and End jump to the first and last. Screen readers hear the number and its unit when a reading is chosen, but not for hover previews.

On the live homepage the head plays as the section arrives. The plate and the block wait until the plate is 40% on screen, then play the same build once, ending on 17. There is no automatic stepping, and nothing loops.
Reduced motion: the final state (17 shown, red at 17, marker filled), with no timers.
addressed: 'The previous design direction looked more proprietary … round two's design direction was good': round 2's layout is back as it was. That means the head, the four big numbers on the hairline cross with their labels and sources, the corner marks, the centre zone and the “Fig. 03 · Four readings, one structure” caption. The extra 'Fig. 03' tag in the top-right corner is gone, because the caption already names the figure.

'Change … the square with dots … an information block or something painted in colors': the dots are gone. In their place is a flat painted block of 100. Red paints the share and a pale ground holds the rest. Nothing is printed inside it: the big number beside it is the one reading (a second “17” inside the block, cut by the red line, read like a glitch). It reads more like a colour chip or a Swiss poster than a chart.

'Equally proprietary, rather than just slapped in': the block is drawn into the plate, not dropped into a hole. The centre's vertical hairline carries on down and hangs the block from the middle of its top edge. The block has its own calibrated scale, whose ticks darken as the red passes them, plus a marker that rides the level and locks when it lands, and a label strip saying what the full block stands for ('100 = the purchase').
It answers the numbers directly. Press or hover any big number and the block re-proportions in one slow move; the marker on the scale rides the level and locks when it lands.

Round 3's honesty is kept. The lede is 'Every one gets blamed on the pipeline. Not one of them moves with more activity.' Sources are as on the live site. Each reading names its own unit in words, and only one reading is on the scale at a time. At 95:5 the pale sliver at the top is labelled '5 buying now', so the split is shown, not just named. The field note 'The 17% window · 5 min' sits quietly in the caption line.

Your standing note on repeated layouts: round 2's tinted band with its 17% · 95:5 · 77% · 53% buttons is not back. The reframe directly above already ends in a band with a toggle, and two in a row is exactly the “heading → plate → band + toggle” repetition you called out in round 3. The four big numbers were already the control (press, hover or arrow keys), so the plate here closes on a plain hairline caption instead.

To keep the block from feeling slapped in, the empty share is drawn with fine 45° section hatching — the drafting convention for a cut surface — so the block reads as a measured specimen rather than a plain bar.
signoff: New decision: at 95:5 the red paints the 95 (the share not buying), with the pale 5 at the top labelled '5 buying now'. Round 3 filled the 5 instead. This keeps red meaning 'the big number you pressed' for all four readings.
notes: Chosen over the alternative (a calibrated horizontal gauge drawn into the cross). The gauge integrated cleverly with the hairlines and was marginally clearer, but at a glance it was still a horizontal progress bar with a tooltip flag. That is close to round 3's '17 / 100' bar, which he called safe and regular-looking, and to the method's approved gantt ruler. It also left the centre under-filled. The painted chip answers his note literally: it keeps round 2's plate and puts a square painted object where the dot square was, so the composition survives, and its red states are the most owned-looking images in the section. Promoted from slot V, with the reviewer's must-fixes and grafts applied. (1) Morph desync: the printed figure is no longer swapped by a timer. Each figure's opacity is computed in CSS from the same registered property that drives the level: clamp(0, 1 − |v − value| × 12, 1). It is gated to the reading shown (data-on) and the one being left (data-from), so it fades as the level leaves and prints as it lands, and no frame shows '95' on a 22% block. The gate is ±8 units, under half the closest pair (77 ↔ 95), so two figures are never on at once. Interrupted morphs and hover previews obey the same rule. Intermediate figures never flash, because only from/on are gated in. (2) The 'Fig. 03' head meta was removed (STORY §9 rule 3). (3) 95:5: the pale remainder carries an 11px mono label '5 buying now' inside the 15px band (ink on --panel), plus a 5px dimension bracket in the block → scale gap. Both ride the level (height = (1 − v) × block) and are gated like the figure. Flagged in signoff. (4) The datum now starts at the block's right keyline (block → gap → node). Nothing is drawn left of the block, so there is no second horizontal under the cross's arm at 17. (5) Hover preview: peek(n) marks the cell (grey rule) and the matching .ac-seg button (.is-peek: --panel-2 fill, 2px --fg-3 top rule, ink text), and clears both on leave or click. (6) The resting 17 now cuts the figure through its lower third: bottom 28px, left 20px, with the level 51px up a ~73px-tall figure. Checked at 1440 in both skins, and it reads as a deliberate knock-out. Graft: an .ac-sr value prefix before each unit line ('17 of 100. ', 'Of 100 in your market: ', '77 of 100. ', '53 of 100. '), so the aria-live readout speaks the number. Registration graft: the frame is now 416px and symmetric about the cross, and the BLOCK (not block plus scale) is centred on the cross's vertical (block 570–870 at 1440). A plumb element continues the vertical hairline from the frame top to the block's top keyline. The entrance draws it at 820ms, then the ground paints down from it. The scale hangs right (ticks 0–10, node at 12, values at 24; '100' ends ≈926px, 27px clear of the 95:5 column). The four registration marks stay on the symmetric frame corners (512/928). Layout is otherwise X's: stage 1393px, head .ac-head, 2×2 at 176px on cols 1–4 / 9–12, and a 72px --panel band with the door aligned to the block's left edge. Claims and so-lines are verbatim from StructuralEvidence.tsx; no count-ups. Known tensions, unchanged from V: about 145 visible words at rest, over STORY's 120 cap, because X's four claims and so-lines are back by his note. The page now has two band toggles (reframe and evidence), because his round-4 note restores round 2's control here. Page context (reframe → evidence → letter) was walked with no console errors; it rests on 17 with no auto-step. ≤760px was verified at 375px: 2×2 numerals at 64px, the chip centred below at 2.4px per unit, the 95:5 label fits its 12px band, and there is no horizontal scroll. Review pass (round 4, adversarial): (a) the standalone entrance no longer opens with 01's ink state rule, square and label visibly retracting for ~600ms before the plate draws: the opening state is now set with the whole section's transitions frozen, including the rule's ::before, which the kit's .ac-cold cannot reach. (b) On the homepage the kit faded the four registration marks on .is-play alone, so they finished fading while the plate was still waiting and popped in ahead of the cross. They are now held until the plate goes. (c) The figure gate was tightened from ×9 to ×12: at ×9 a 95 ↔ 77 move showed both figures at ~19% for ~60ms at its midpoint. (d) The demo was re-timed to 0.65s moves and settles at ≈ 5.9s, inside the 6s target (demoMs 6000). (e) The field-note door is now stone (--fg-2), inking on hover/focus, so the band's control stays its loudest element. (f) aria-live is muted for hover previews and restored for real selections. COHERENCE PASS (round 4, supersedes the lines above where they disagree): (1) the band's segmented control is removed (markup, CSS and the JS wiring); the numerals are the only control, and the reframe keeps the page's one band + toggle (STORY §0 cap restored; the "two band toggles" tension above is resolved). (2) The band is now a caption row: a 1px --line top rule (the plate's base line, where the cross's vertical lands), 14px air, caption left, field-note door on the block's left edge; no --panel fill. The last ink now sits ~128px above the cut, so the seam matches every other section (was ~156px under the 72px band). (3) The printed figure inside the block (.fig-n, ink + paper copies, and its level gate) is removed: it doubled the 176px numeral and the resting level sliced it. Stage 1393 → 1361px.
